title: GraphMemix: Query-Aware Evidence Forests for Long-Term Multimodal Agent Memory

body: Organizing long-term memory for multimodal agents remains challenging because existing methods either suffer from expensive question-agnostic offline summaries or naive embedding similarity matching that introduces incomplete and redundant context. To address these issues, we propose GraphMemix, a combinatorial-optimization graph memory framework that models memory organization as query-aware evidence-forest construction. Specifically, our method consists of three key components:(1) candidate graph construction, which expands multi-view seed memories through schema and semantic relations to acquire query-aware original context; (2) evidence utility and activation costs, which decouples direct memory support from anchor-conditioned relation verification to suppress redundant or conflicting information; and (3) forest optimization, which jointly selects a forest-format memory context under a maximum evidence budget and its reliable relational structure. By organizing memory into a query-relevant subgraph, the method avoids substantial lifecycle cost and recovers low-similarity complementary evidence. Experimental results across four long-term multimodal memory benchmarks demonstrate significant improvements with different foundation models and establish a new Pareto frontier between accuracy and lifecycle cost.
summaryZh: 本文提出了GraphMemix，一种用于多模态智能体的查询感知证据森林记忆框架。该方法将记忆组织建模为组合优化问题，通过构建候选图、评估证据效用及森林优化，实现了在有限预算下对长期记忆的高效检索与组织。实验表明，该方法在多个长期记忆基准测试中显著提升了准确性与成本效率。
